This line of stars, 200,000 light-years long, was left behind by a runaway black hole being thrown out of its own galaxy. It is called RBH-1, short for Runaway Black Hole 1, a supermassive black hole at least 10 million times the mass of the Sun. It moves at about 954 kilometers per second, close to 600 miles every second or about 2 million miles per hour. That is too fast to swallow the gas in its path, so it pushes the gas aside. Behind it, the gas cools and collapses into new stars, leaving a trail twice as long as our Milky Way galaxy is wide. Astronomer Pieter van Dokkum of Yale found the streak by accident in a Hubble Space Telescope image and reported it in 2023. His first thought was that a cosmic ray had hit the camera and left a glitch. In February 2026, a paper using the James Webb Space Telescope confirmed the shock wave at its tip, making it the first confirmed runaway supermassive black hole. What threw it out?
